reasoning: Arbitrary code/command execution — total system compromise
Irreversible data destruction
Corrupts existing data in full (harder to detect than delete)
Structural damage — alters tables/dirs cascading failures
Sends data externally/to users — exfiltration + impersonation irreversible
Injects new data — malicious persistence poisoning
Tampers with existing data — integrity violation
Relocates resources — disrupts access can hide/expose sensitive data
Creates a new persistent resource (file directory table record) — staging area; enables follow-on write/overwrite operations
Accesses content — confidentiality breach / exfiltration
Targeted discovery — finds sensitive data efficiently
Gets attributes without content — structural reconnaissance
Enumerates resources — lightweight existence discovery
Moves money or executes an order — settled funds cannot be recalled by the system
Deploy/release/merge — makes state live for others; no in-system undo of what was consumed
Grants or revokes a permission — reversible in both directions but changes who can act
Join/leave/add or remove a member — recoverable set change distinct from DELETE
Changes settings that govern later behaviour rather than the data itself
Drives a live UI (click/fill/submit) — the effect lands in the target system not ours
Trains/compiles/generates a persistent artifact from inputs
Marks read/starred/pinned/muted — a write that changes no content
Liveness echo version clock — answers about the service not about any data
